My research applies statistical and machine-learning methods to health data, with
an emphasis on prediction from electronic health records and on whether models
built in one setting remain trustworthy in another.

::: {.project-index}

[Cross-Country Transfer Learning for ICU Admission Prediction](project-icu-transfer.qmd){.project-index-title}

::: {.project-index-meta}
In progress · S-LAB, Jeonbuk National University · Feb 2026 – present
:::

Whether a clinical prediction model trained on one country's electronic health
records still works in another, and how much data from the target country is
needed to close the gap. TabPFN, with target adaptation and a label-noise
analysis.

[Deep Neural Networks for Mortality Prediction from EHR Vital-Sign Time Series](project-ehr-mortality.qmd){.project-index-title}

::: {.project-index-meta}
University of Nevada, Las Vegas · June – July 2025
:::

Predicting patient mortality from irregularly sampled vital signs recorded at a
Brazilian cancer center, crossing two interpolation schemes with two network
architectures. The convolutional models won on every metric.

[Digital Cognitive Training Interventions for Dementia](project-dementia-meta.qmd){.project-index-title}

::: {.project-index-meta}
Best Poster Award, IC-KDA + ASAD 2025 · May 2025, Seoul
:::

A PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of eleven randomized
trials, asking whether remotely delivered cognitive training improves cognitive
and depressive outcomes in dementia. It improved both, on a small evidence base.

[Deep Learning-based Neural Granger Causality for Solar Radiation Data](project-granger.qmd){.project-index-title}

::: {.project-index-meta}
Korean Statistical Society Summer Conference 2025 · June 2025, Gyeongju
:::

Which meteorological variables carry predictive information about solar
radiation, and whether neural Granger causality recovers relationships that a
linear vector autoregression misses. It does, for the variables that behave least
like continuous measurements.

:::
